annotation.title_clean: How Ethical Issues Raised by Human–Robot Interaction can Impact the Intention to use the Robot?
annotation.title_en: How Ethical Issues Raised by Human–Robot Interaction can Impact the Intention to use the Robot?
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Etemad-Sajadi, R.; Soussan, A.; Schöpfer, T.
annotation.summary_en: Empirical study (n=341, SEM) using a video of the Pepper robot to test how ethical attributes (safety, trust, social cues, autonomy, responsibility, privacy, job replacement) affect intention to use service robots. Replacement of labor is the most salient concern; social cues, trust and safety most strongly drive intention to use.
key_provisions_or_claims: Replacement and its labor implications is the most important ethical issue for respondents.
Social cues, trust and safety have the strongest impact on intention to use service robots.
Study of 341 respondents using SEM after viewing a Pepper robot video.
Responsibility for robot errors and privacy/GDPR compliance are identified as open ethical concerns.
Focuses on social service robots, not military, medical or industrial robots.
